question: What does ALARM 14 mean on the Danfoss VLT AQUA Drive FC 202, and how do I fix it?
ground_truth: ALARM 14 is an earth (ground) fault: current is flowing from the output phases to ground, either in the motor cable or in the motor itself. Remove power and repair the ground fault, check the motor and cables with a megohmmeter (resistance to ground), and perform a current sensor test.
evidence: There is current from the output phases to ground, either in the cable between the frequency converter and the motor, or in the motor itself.

question: What does the LF fault mean on a Yaskawa GA500 drive?
ground_truth: LF is Output Phase Loss: phase loss on the output side of the drive. Causes include a disconnected motor cable, a broken motor coil winding, loose output terminal screws, a motor rated below 5% of the drive current, trying to run a single-phase motor, or a damaged output transistor. Fix the wiring or motor, tighten terminals, and do a Fault Reset; L8-07 enables or disables LF detection.
evidence: The drive detects this fault if phase loss occurs on the output side of the drive.

question: What does fault F07 mean on the Aquavar SOLO2 controller?
ground_truth: F07 (7 blinks) is a Temperature fault: the ambient temperature is outside the rating, above 122 °F (50 °C) or below -4 °F (-20 °C). Check for a fan failure (the fan turns on at 140 °F / 60 °C inside the controller). The controller restarts automatically once the temperature is acceptable.
evidence: High ambient temperature. The maximum ambient temperature rating is 122º F (50º C).

question: What does 7 flashes mean on the Franklin Electric SubDrive?
ground_truth: 7 flashes is Overheated Drive, caused by high ambient temperature, direct sunlight or blocked airflow. The heat sink has exceeded its max rated temperature and must drop below 85 °C to restart; check for a blocked or failed fan or ambient above 50 °C, and replace the fan or relocate the drive.
evidence: Drive heat sink has exceeded max rated temperature, needs to drop below 85 °C to restart

question: What is CPF06 on the Yaskawa GA500 and how is it fixed?
ground_truth: CPF06 is an EEPROM Memory Data Error. It happens if the drive was powered off while a communication option card was writing a parameter (fix: set A1-03 = 2220 or 3330 to initialize the drive), or from an EEPROM peripheral circuit error (re-energize; if it stays, replace the control board or drive).
evidence: The drive power supply was de-energized while a communication option card entered a parameter Write command.

question: What does WARNING 23 mean on the Danfoss FC 202?
ground_truth: WARNING 23 is an Internal fan fault: the fan monitor detected the internal fan is not running or not mounted. Check the fan resistance and the soft charge fuses. The fan warning can be disabled in parameter 14-53 Fan Monitor.
evidence: WARNING 23, Internal fan fault

question: My Aquavar SOLO2 display says STOP and the status light is solid green. Why won't the pump run?
ground_truth: Solid green with STOP means the Run/Stop input is open, which forces the pump to stop. Check the device controlling the Run/Stop input (float or pressure switch) and its wiring; the input must be closed (the factory jumper in place) for the pump to run, and its wiring must be kept at least 12 inches from power wires.
evidence: indicates that the Run/ Stop input is open which forces the pump to stop.

question: The Aquavar pump-mounted controller keeps shutting down because the inverter gets too hot. What should I check and how do I reset it?
ground_truth: That is the Overtemp Inverter error, normally caused by poor cooling of the aluminum heat sink on the bottom of the controller. Check the heat sink for dirt, check airflow from the motor fan and the ambient temperature. Once the temperature is back in range, reset by turning the controller off for at least 30 seconds.
evidence: This is normally caused by a lack of cooling of the aluminum heat sink on the bottom of the AQUAVAR controller.

question: The Aquavar controller stops the pump when the suction tank level drops. What message does it show and what should I check?
ground_truth: It shows Lack of Water: a switch indicated that incoming water pressure or suction tank level fell below the pump's required NPSH. Check suction conditions and that the pressure or float switch works; the pump restarts automatically when suction returns to normal. The message also appears if terminals 6 and 7 on terminal block X1 are not bridged.
evidence: This message will also appear if terminals 6 and 7 on terminal block X1 are not bridged.

question: After a pipe burst, my Aquavar SOLO2 shut the pump off and it will not restart by itself. Why?
ground_truth: That is the Low Pressure Cut-Off fault (F09, 9 blinks): pressure was 20 PSI below the set point for 30 seconds, for example from a broken pipe or a tripped relief valve. It does not clear automatically; fix the cause and do a System Reset or cycle power for 1 minute. If such a drop is normal for the system, switch Low Pressure Cut-Off off.
evidence: Pressure 20 PSI below set point for 30 seconds.

question: My Franklin SubDrive pump keeps running and won't shut off. What should I check?
ground_truth: That is the Run On / Won't Shut Down condition (flashing green). Possible causes: pressure sensor placement and setting, tank pre-charge pressure, impeller damage, a leaky system, or a pump sized so it can't build enough head. Check frequency at low flow (the pressure setting may be too close to pump max head), verify precharge at 70% (up to 85% for larger tanks), and verify the system builds and holds pressure.
evidence: Verify precharge at 70% if tank size is larger than minimum, increase precharge (up to 85%)

question: What does oL2 mean on the Yaskawa GA500?
ground_truth: oL2 is Drive Overload (not motor overload like oL1). Causes include too large a load, too-short accel/decel or cycle times, a V/f pattern that doesn't fit the motor, a drive capacity that is too small (replace with a larger drive), overload at low speed, too large torque compensation gain, wrong speed search settings, or input phase loss.
evidence: The drive capacity is too small.

question: On the Yaskawa GA500, what is Uv2?
ground_truth: Uv2 is Control Power Undervoltage: the control power supply voltage dropped. Causes: L2-02 power loss ride-through time was increased without the momentary power loss recovery unit connected (connect it), or a drive hardware problem (re-energize; if it stays, replace the control board or drive).
evidence: The drive detects this error if the control power supply voltage decreases.

question: What causes WARNING/ALARM 12 on the Danfoss FC 202 and how do I clear it?
ground_truth: Alarm 12 is Torque limit: torque exceeded parameter 4-16 (motor mode) or 4-17 (generator mode). If it happens during ramp-up, extend the ramp-up time; during ramp-down, extend the ramp-down time; while running, possibly increase the torque limit if safe, and check the application for excessive current draw.
evidence: If the motor torque limit is exceeded during ramp-up, extend the ramp-up time.

question: What does fault F02 mean on the Aquavar SOLO2?
ground_truth: F02 (2 blinks) is Dry Well, no water or loss of prime. Causes: well water level below the pump suction inlet, a plugged suction screen, a restriction between pump and pressure sensor, an air-bound pump, or wrong Maximum Speed or Motor Overload (SFA) switch settings. It can restart automatically with Progressive or Fixed Time restart, or be reset by pressing both buttons or cycling power.
evidence: Water supply level in well falls below suction inlet of pump.

question: What does alarm 4 mean on the Danfoss FC 202?
ground_truth: WARNING/ALARM 4 is Mains phase loss: a phase is missing on the supply side or the mains voltage imbalance is too high (it can also mean a fault in the input rectifier). Check the supply voltage and supply currents to the frequency converter. Behaviour is set in parameter 14-12 Function at Mains Imbalance.
evidence: A phase is missing on the supply side, or the mains voltage imbalance is too high.

question: What does a 5-blink fault mean on the Aquavar SOLO2?
ground_truth: 5 blinks (F05) is Short Circuit, from an electrical failure of the motor or of the wiring between controller and motor. Do not reset it more than twice without fixing the cause. Cycle power to verify; if it persists, remove the motor wires and check wiring and motor phase to phase and phase to ground (insulation and winding resistance tests).
evidence: Repeated exposure to Short Circuit conditions can damage the controller.

question: danfoss fc202 showing A13 on the display, what does that mean
ground_truth: A13 is alarm 13, Over current: the inverter peak current limit (about 200% of rated current) was exceeded; the warning lasts about 1.5 s, then the drive trips. Shock loading or fast acceleration with high-inertia loads can cause it. Remove power and check the motor shaft turns, check the motor size matches the drive, and check parameters 1-20 to 1-25.
evidence: The inverter peak current limit (approximately 200% of the rated current) is exceeded.

question: yaskawa ga-500 says OH1, what do i do
ground_truth: oH1 is Heatsink Overheat: the heatsink temperature passed the oH1 detection level (set by o2-04 drive model). Measure ambient temperature, increase airflow in the panel, add cooling, remove nearby heat sources, reduce the load, and decrease C6-02 carrier frequency. Do a Fault Reset afterwards.
evidence: o2-04 [Drive Model (KVA) Selection] determines the oH1 detection level.

question: aquavar solo 2 shows F-03 on the display
ground_truth: F03 (3 blinks) is a Sensor Fault: a disconnected sensor or sensor cable lead, a broken or miswired sensor cable, a failed sensor (should read 0.5 to 4.5 VDC between black and white wires), or a vacuum of 17 inches Hg or more on the transducer. Also check the Transducer Jumper position. It restarts automatically when the signal is back in tolerance.
evidence: A vacuum on the sensor (transducer) of 17" Hg or more will cause a sensor fault, eliminate the vacuum.

question: With Progressive restart on the Aquavar SOLO2, how long does it wait after the first dry well fault, and after the fifth?
ground_truth: Progressive reset waits 1 minute after the first dry well fault and 60 minutes after the fifth (and any later) fault; in between it is 10, 20 and 30 minutes for the 2nd, 3rd and 4th.
evidence: Reset Time 1 1 minute ... 5 and greater 60 minutes

question: What does oH mean on the Yaskawa GA500, and what must I do after replacing a stopped cooling fan?
ground_truth: oH is Heatsink Overheat: the heatsink temperature is above L8-02 [Overheat Alarm Level], from high ambient temperature, too heavy a load, or a stopped internal cooling fan. After replacing the fan, set o4-03 = 0 [Fan Operation Time Setting = 0 h].
evidence: The drive detects this fault if the heatsink temperature of the drive is more than the value set in L8-02. ... The internal cooling fan of the drive stopped. 1. Use the procedures in this manual to replace the cooling fan. 2. Set o4-03 = 0 [Fan Operation Time Setting = 0 h].

question: The Franklin SubDrive is flashing 6 times. What two faults can that be, and how do I tell them apart?
ground_truth: 6 flashes is either Short Circuit or Over Current. If the fault appears immediately after power-up it is a short circuit (loose connection, defective cable, splice or motor); if it appears while the motor is running it is over current, from loose debris trapped in the pump (check the pump).
evidence: When fault is indicated immediately after power-up, short circuit due to loose connection, defective cable, splice or motor ... When fault is indicated while motor is running, over current due to loose debris trapped in pump
